Although TOU never maximizes production cost savings, it might provide the most value over a wide range of participation rates after accounting for implementation costs. Improved forecasting increases the EVMC participation levels at which price-responsive dispatch mechanisms are competitive with DLC. Table 4 shows DLC is the highest-value mechanism only at high participation rates, specifically 45% LDV participation for within-session flexibility and 27% LDV participation and above for within-week flexibility. However, price-responsive mechanisms can still be value-competitive with DLC, even when they yield lower savings. DLC requires frequent two-way communication and coordination, which implies higher enablement costs. For DLC to be the preferred mechanism, its additional savings must exceed its additional costs when compared to alternatives. To estimate how much value could be extracted from the higher costs of DLC, it is instructive to quantify differences between DLC savings and preferred price-responsive mechanism savings. For within-session flexibility at 45% LDV participation and within-week flexibility at 27% LDV participation, the TOU mechanism, although not preferred overall, is the preferred price-responsive mechanism and only reduces savings compared to DLC-LE by $3/veh-yr or 13% (DLC $23 vs. TOU $20/veh-yr) and $12/veh-yr or 27% (DLC $45 vs. TOU $33/veh-yr), respectively (Table 4). This suggests that incremental enablement costs for within-session DLC compared to a well-designed TOU tariff must be tens of dollars per vehicle-year or less to be value-competitive with TOU rates. A similar result holds for within-week DLC, but over a narrower band of participation levels, as only DLC is able to effectively schedule the within-week charging flexibility of 45% of the LDV fleet to achieve overall production cost savings of nearly 10% (Figure 5). A TOU rate can also be value-competitive with RTP. TOU rates are coarser and updated much less frequently than RTPs, which means communications, controls, and response forecasting can be simpler, less costly to implement, and less sensitive to communication disruptions. And although RTP is the highest-value mechanism at low participation rates, as participation rates increase, the flattened TOU responses implemented in our study become preferred. TOU (perfect-foresight) outperforms RTP (perfect-foresight) in total and incremental savings value for 27%–45% LDV participation for within-week flexibility and at 45% LDV participation for within-session flexibility (Figure 5). And although RTP responses can greatly increase maximum system-level ramp rates, TOU reduces maximum system-level ramp rates compared to the unmanaged scenario in all but one scenario (Table A.2, also see Figure 4 for the 27% LDV within-week scenario).
